title: Empirical degradation map for KV cache lossy compaction (FP8/INT8/INT4)
creator: Ava Chen
description: Goal: Build an empirical degradation matrix that maps per-layer and per-token quality impact vs VRAM savings for three lossy KV cache compaction formats (FP8, INT8, INT4) under continuous batching. We will identify safe operating regions and automated fallback triggers to preserve user-facing quality while lowering memory footprint and increasing batch sizes. This ticket covers experiment design, data collection, analysis, and a short proposal for runtime policy changes.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A reproducible benchmark harness that runs at-scale continuous-batching workloads against a set of representative models (Llama-like 13B, 30B and an instruction-tuned 7B) and outputs per-layer quality vs memory tradeoffs. 2) A degradation matrix (CSV) and visual heatmap showing metrics (perplexity delta, instruction-response pass rate, embedding cosine drop, hallucination indicator) for FP8/INT8/INT4. 3) A short recommendations doc with: safe quantization profiles, per-request fallback thresholds, and expected VRAM reduction numbers. 4) A follow-up runtime PR proposal (RFC) that details policy primitives required for rollout.
experimental_plan:
- Baselines: run continuous batching harness with default FP16 KV storage, record VRAM, p50/p95 latency, throughput tokens/s, and quality metrics on held-out eval prompts.
- Variants: per-layer FP8, per-tensor INT8, block INT4, and hybrid mixes (top-N layers full precision + bottom layers quantized).
- Calibration: test symmetric vs asymmetric quantization, per-shard scale tables, and residual-compensation (store small per-key residuals in FP16).
- Data: use 10k evaluation prompts spanning short chats, long context math, and retrieval-augmented responses.
- Runs: sweep batch sizes (1, 4, 16, 64) and sequence lengths (128, 512, 2048).
- Observables: collect per-token perplexity delta, response-level pass/fail for instruction tests, embedding cosine similarity drop, and safety/hallucination flag rate.
- Automation: harness writes a single CSV row per run; analysis notebook will compute per-layer sensitivity scores and cumulative quality cost for memory savings.
metrics_and_observables: Quality metrics: delta perplexity (relative), instr-response pass rate (%), embedding cosine similarity (mean), hallucination flag rate (proxy). Runtime metrics: GPU VRAM used (MB), peak allocator fragmentation (%), p50/p95 latency (ms), steady-state throughput (tokens/s), batching efficiency (tokens/second per GB). Business metrics: expected cost reduction per 100k tokens and projected improvement in concurrent sessions per GPU.
risks_and_mitigation:
- Risk: INT4 artifacts cause instruction compliance regressions. Mitigation: conservative hybrid profile and per-request fallback to FP16 when instruction pass rate for a model falls below threshold.
- Risk: quantization increases variance across seeds and prompts. Mitigation: run multi-seed experiments and report confidence intervals; prefer quantization profiles with lower variance.
- Risk: decoder kernels regress throughput on certain GPUs for INT4. Mitigation: include kernel perf checks and detect slowdown >5% to gate rollout.
- Risk: increased memory fragmentation with many small residuals. Mitigation: evaluate storing residuals in contiguous slab and benchmark fragmentation metrics.
